arxiv-1602-02717.title: REGULARITY PROPERTIES OF FIBER DERIVATIVES ASSOCIATED WITH HIGHER-ORDER MECHANICAL SYSTEMS Thanks: e - mail : math.pedro.daniel.prieto@gmail.com
arxiv-1602-02717.creator: Leonardo Colombo
arxiv-1602-02717.description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Leonardo Colombo. The aim of this work is to study fiber derivatives associated to Lagrangian and Hamiltonian functions describing the dynamics of a higher-order autonomous dynamical system. More precisely, given a function in T ∗ ​ T ( k − 1 ) ​ Q T^{*}T^{(k-1)}Q , we find necessary and sufficient conditions for such a function to describe the dynamics of a k k th-order autonomous dynamical system, thus being a k k th-order Hamiltonian function.

arxiv-2107-05470.title: Enlightening the CSL model landscape in inflation
arxiv-2107-05470.creator: Gabriel León, Gabriel R. Bengochea
arxiv-2107-05470.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Gabriel León, Gabriel R. Bengochea. We propose a novel realization for the natural extrapolation of the continuous spontaneous localization (CSL) model, in order to account for the origin of primordial inhomogeneities during inflation. This particular model is based on three main elements: (i) the semiclassical gravity framework, (ii) a collapse-generating operator associated to a relativistic invariant scalar of the energy-momentum tensor, and (iii) an extension of the CSL parameter(s) as a function of the spacetime curvature.

arxiv-2203-07079.title: Strategy Complexity of Point Payoff, Mean Payoff and Total Payoff Objectives in Countable MDPs
arxiv-2203-07079.creator: Richard Mayr, Eric Munday
arxiv-2203-07079.description: Abstract . We study countably infinite Markov decision processes (MDPs) with real-valued transition rewards. Every infinite run induces the following sequences of payoffs: 1. Point payoff (the sequence of directly seen transition rewards), 2. Mean payoff (the sequence of the sums of all rewards so far, divided by the number of steps), and 3.

arxiv-2206-12177.title: A non-lorentzian primer Thanks: EMPG-22-08
arxiv-2206-12177.creator: Eric A. Bergshoeff, José M. Figueroa-O’Farrill, Joaquim Gomis
arxiv-2206-12177.description: Abstract . We review both the kinematics and dynamics of non-lorentzian theories and their associated geometries. First, we introduce non-lorentzian kinematical spacetimes and their symmetry algebras. Next, we construct actions describing the particle dynamics in some of these kinematical spaces using the method of nonlinear realisations. We explain the relation with the coadjoint orbit method.

arxiv-2212-02261.title: A review on the protocols for the synthesis of proteinoids Journal: Journal
arxiv-2212-02261.creator: Saksham Sharma , Panagiotis Mougoyannis, Giuseppe Tarabella, Andrew Adamatzky
arxiv-2212-02261.description: Abstract Protocells are a type of synthetic cells, which, if engineered to have properties similar to a natural cell, can have immense applications in synthetic biology and bioengineering communities. Proteinoids are one of the leading contenders for protocells discovered by Sidney H. Fox in 1950s as the protein-like molecules which are made out of amino acids.

arxiv-2305-04222.title: Branching Place Bisimilarity
arxiv-2305-04222.creator: Roberto Gorrieri
arxiv-2305-04222.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Roberto Gorrieri. Place bisimilarity ∼ p \sim_{p} is a behavioral equivalence for finite Petri nets, proposed in [ 1 ] and proved decidable in [ 17 ] . In this paper we propose an extension to finite Petri nets with silent moves of the place bisimulation idea, yielding branching place bisimilarity ≈ p \approx_{p} , following the intuition of branching bisimilarity [ 9 ] on labeled transition systems.

arxiv-2309-08460.title: Explaining Search Result Stances to Opinionated People
arxiv-2309-08460.creator: Zhangyi Wu, Tim Draws, Federico Cau, Francesco Barile, Alisa Rieger, Nava Tintarev
arxiv-2309-08460.description: Abstract People use web search engines to find information before forming opinions, which can lead to practical decisions with different levels of impact. The cognitive effort of search can leave opinionated users vulnerable to cognitive biases, e.g., the confirmation bias . In this paper, we investigate whether stance labels and their explanations can help users consume more diverse search results.

arxiv-2309-11725.title: FluentEditor: text-based speech editing by considering acoustic and prosody consistency
arxiv-2309-11725.creator: Rui Liu, Jiatian Xi, Ziyue Jiang, Haizhou Li
arxiv-2309-11725.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Rui Liu, Jiatian Xi, Ziyue Jiang, Haizhou Li. Text-based speech editing (TSE) techniques are designed to enable users to edit the output audio by modifying the input text transcript instead of the audio itself. Despite much progress in neural network-based TSE techniques, the current techniques have focused on reducing the difference between the generated speech segment and the reference target in the editing region, ignoring its local and global fluency in the context and original utterance.

arxiv-2403-04160.title: Improving Retrieval in Theme-specific Applications using a Corpus Topical Taxonomy Conference: Proceedings of the ACM Web Conference 2024; May 13–17, 2024; Singapore, Singapore Proceedings of the ACM Web Conference 2024 (WWW ’24), May 13–17, 2024, Singapore, Singapore DOI: 10.1145/3589334.3645512 IS
arxiv-2403-04160.creator: SeongKu Kang, Shivam Agarwal, Bowen Jin, Dongha Lee, Hwanjo Yu, Jiawei Han
arxiv-2403-04160.description: Abstract . Document retrieval has greatly benefited from the advancements of large-scale pre-trained language models (PLMs). However, their effectiveness is often limited in theme-specific applications for specialized areas or industries, due to unique terminologies, incomplete contexts of user queries, and specialized search intents.

arxiv-2412-17971.title: Functional independent component analysis by choice of norm: a framework for near-perfect classification
arxiv-2412-17971.creator: Marc Vidal, Marc Leman, Ana M. Aguilera
arxiv-2412-17971.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Marc Vidal, Marc Leman, Ana M. Aguilera. We develop a theory for functional independent component analysis in an infinite-dimensional framework using Sobolev spaces that accommodate smoother functions. The notion of penalized kurtosis is introduced motivated by Silverman’s method for smoothing principal components. This approach allows for a classical definition of independent components obtained via projection onto the eigenfunctions of a smoothed kurtosis operator mapping a whitened functional random variable.

arxiv-2501-16726.title: Bridging Neural Networks and Wireless Systems with MIMO-OFDM Semantic Communications PubID: pubid: 0000–0000/00$00.00 © 2021 IEEE
arxiv-2501-16726.creator: Hanju Yoo, Dongha Choi, Yonghwi Kim, Yoontae Kim, Songkuk Kim, Chan-Byoung Chae, Robert W. Heath, Jr
arxiv-2501-16726.description: Abstract Semantic communications aim to enhance transmission efficiency by jointly optimizing source coding, channel coding, and modulation. While prior research has demonstrated promising performance in simulations, real-world implementations often face significant challenges, including noise variability and nonlinear distortions, leading to performance gaps.

arxiv-2507-22598.title: The Multiconfigurational Ground State of a Diradicaloid Characterized at the Atomic Scale
arxiv-2507-22598.creator: Elia Turco, Lara Tejerina, Gonçalo Catarina, Andres Ortega-Guerrero, Nils Krane, Leo Gross, Michal Juríček, Shantanu Mishra
arxiv-2507-22598.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Elia Turco, Lara Tejerina, Gonçalo Catarina, Andres Ortega-Guerrero, Nils Krane, Leo Gross, Michal Juríček, Shantanu Mishra. We report the tip-induced generation and scanning probe characterization of a singlet diradicaloid, consisting of two phenalenyl units connected by an sp-hybridized C 4 chain, on an ultrathin insulating NaCl surface. The bond-order contrast along the C 4 chain measured by atomic force microscopy and mapping of charge-state transitions by scanning tunneling microscopy, in conjunction with multiconfigurational calculations, reveal that the molecule exhibits a many-body ground state.

arxiv-2602-16696.creator: Huan Souza, Pankaj Mehta
arxiv-2602-16696.description: Abstract Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data exhibit strong and reproducible statistical structure. This has motivated the development of large-scale foundation models, such as TranscriptFormer, that use transformer-based architectures to learn a generative model for gene expression by embedding genes into a latent vector space.
